about: Windows Security log facts for the trusted reference block (D39, D40) and validator check 9 (D42). Every entry is a short paraphrase of Microsoft's documentation, with a source. Codes missing from this table fail closed. Extend by hand, with a source for each entry.

4624.name: An account was successfully logged on
4624.meaning: A logon session was created successfully. The Logon Type field says how the logon happened.
4624.source: Verified against Microsoft Learn, Windows security auditing, 'Event 4624(S): An account was successfully logged on'

4625.name: An account failed to log on
4625.meaning: A logon attempt failed. The Status and SubStatus fields give the reason. An attempt against a locked-out account is also logged as 4625, with Status 0xC0000234.
4625.source: Verified against Microsoft Learn, Windows security auditing, 'Event 4625(F): An account failed to log on'

4634.name: An account was logged off
4634.meaning: A logon session ended. It is generated when a logon session is destroyed.
4634.source: Verified against Microsoft Learn, Windows security auditing, 'Event 4634(S): An account was logged off'

4648.name: A logon was attempted using explicit credentials
4648.meaning: A process tried to log on with credentials supplied explicitly, instead of the current user's credentials.
4648.source: Verified against Microsoft Learn, Windows security auditing, 'Event 4648(S): A logon was attempted using explicit credentials'

4672.name: Special privileges assigned to new logon
4672.meaning: A new logon was given sensitive privileges (administrator-level rights such as debugging or taking ownership). Every SYSTEM logon triggers it, so it is high-volume and not suspicious on its own.
4672.source: Verified against Microsoft Learn, Windows security auditing, 'Event 4672(S): Special privileges assigned to new logon'

4688.name: A new process has been created
4688.meaning: A process was started. The command line is recorded only when the extra audit policy for it is on.
4688.source: Verified against Microsoft Learn, Windows security auditing, 'Event 4688(S): A new process has been created'

4720.name: A user account was created
4720.meaning: A new local or domain user account was created.
4720.source: Verified against Microsoft Learn, Windows security auditing, 'Event 4720(S): A user account was created'

4740.name: A user account was locked out
4740.meaning: An account was locked out. It records the moment the account becomes locked. Later failed logons against that account are event 4625 with Status 0xC0000234.
4740.source: Verified against Microsoft Learn, Windows security auditing, 'Event 4740(S): A user account was locked out'

2.name: Interactive
2.meaning: A user logged on at the keyboard and screen of this computer (the console).
2.source: Verified against Microsoft Learn, 'Event 4624(S)', Logon Type table

3.name: Network
3.meaning: A user or computer logged on to this computer from the network (for example a file share).
3.source: Verified against Microsoft Learn, 'Event 4624(S)', Logon Type table

4.name: Batch
4.meaning: A batch logon: a process runs on behalf of a user without their direct intervention.
4.source: Verified against Microsoft Learn, 'Event 4624(S)', Logon Type table

5.name: Service
5.meaning: A service was started by the Service Control Manager.
5.source: Verified against Microsoft Learn, 'Event 4624(S)', Logon Type table

7.name: Unlock
7.source: Verified against Microsoft Learn, 'Event 4624(S)', Logon Type table

8.name: NetworkCleartext
8.meaning: A user logged on from the network, and the password was passed to the authentication package in unhashed form.
8.source: Verified against Microsoft Learn, 'Event 4624(S)', Logon Type table

9.name: NewCredentials
9.meaning: A caller cloned its current token and supplied new credentials for outbound network connections. The local identity stays the same.
9.source: Verified against Microsoft Learn, 'Event 4624(S)', Logon Type table

10.name: RemoteInteractive
10.meaning: A user logged on to this computer remotely with Terminal Services or Remote Desktop.
10.source: Verified against Microsoft Learn, 'Event 4624(S)', Logon Type table

11.name: CachedInteractive
11.meaning: A user logged on with network credentials stored locally on the computer. The domain controller was not contacted.
11.source: Verified against Microsoft Learn, 'Event 4624(S)', Logon Type table

0xC000006D.name: STATUS_LOGON_FAILURE
0xC000006D.meaning: Logon failure: bad username or authentication information. Commonly paired with a more specific Sub Status (for example 0xC0000064 or 0xC000006A).
0xC000006D.source: Verified against Microsoft Learn, 'Event 4625(F)', Status and Sub Status table

0xC000006A.name: STATUS_WRONG_PASSWORD
0xC000006A.meaning: The user name is correct but the password is wrong.
0xC000006A.source: Verified against Microsoft Learn, 'Event 4625(F)', Status and Sub Status table

0xC0000064.name: STATUS_NO_SUCH_USER
0xC0000064.meaning: The user name does not exist.
0xC0000064.source: Verified against Microsoft Learn, 'Event 4625(F)', Status and Sub Status table

0xC0000234.name: STATUS_ACCOUNT_LOCKED_OUT
0xC0000234.source: MS-SAMR 2.2.1.15 STATUS_ Codes (STATUS_ACCOUNT_LOCKED_OUT); the 'Event 4625(F)' page also lists the failure reason 'Account locked out'. Not in the 4625 Status table

0xC0000072.name: STATUS_ACCOUNT_DISABLED
0xC0000072.source: Verified against Microsoft Learn, 'Event 4625(F)', Status and Sub Status table

0xC000015B.name: STATUS_LOGON_TYPE_NOT_GRANTED
0xC000015B.meaning: The user has not been granted the requested logon type (logon right) on this machine.
aliases: not been granted the requested logon type
0xC000015B.source: Verified against Microsoft Learn, 'Event 4625(F)', Status and Sub Status table

0xC0000071.name: STATUS_PASSWORD_EXPIRED
0xC0000071.source: NTSTATUS values list, MS-ERREF 2.3.1 (STATUS_PASSWORD_EXPIRED). Not in the 4625 Status table

0xC0000193.name: STATUS_ACCOUNT_EXPIRED
0xC0000193.meaning: The account itself has expired (account expiration, not password expiry).
0xC0000193.source: Verified against Microsoft Learn, 'Event 4625(F)', Status and Sub Status table

password_spraying.meaning: Many different accounts, each tried only once or twice from one source address: the shape of password spraying.

brute_force.meaning: Many attempts against a single account from one source address: the shape of password guessing (brute force).

undetermined.meaning: The failed logons from this source address fit neither pattern. Do not name either technique from this group alone.
